api_cost.charged: unconditionally (incurred spend, including examples sent to a human)
api_cost.note: ModernBERT-base (149M) inference, amortized GPU rental. HALF MEASURED, HALF ESTIMATED, and the split matters: the THROUGHPUT is measured — the slowest of the three seed runs, tier_b1_modernbert_sc, logged wall_clock_seconds 15154.9 for eval_sample_size 104443 (0.1451 s/complaint, 6.89 complaints/s, inference_hardware mps) — while the PRICE is an estimate, $0.50 per GPU-hour, taken as the order-of-magnitude community-cloud rate for the NVIDIA RTX A6000 these checkpoints were trained on. 0.1451 s x $0.50/3600 s = $2.0153e-05 per complaint ($0.0202 per 1,000). Two conservatism notes, both stated rather than corrected for: the logged wall clock is the WHOLE harness run (CAL inference for temperature scaling, TEST inference, and the 1,000-replicate bootstrap), so it overstates pure inference; and pricing MPS-measured throughput at a rented-A6000 rate mixes two machines. Both push the figure UP, which is the safe direction for a tier whose cost advantage is the claim. It is ~5 orders of magnitude below the c_misroute term at any realistic error rate, so no frontier claim turns on the rental rate.

bootstrap.method: percentile [2.5, 97.5] over resampled example indices (one integers(0, n, size=n) draw per replicate)

human_assumption: Examples routed to the human queue pay c_human and are not charged the misroute cost: human resolution is assumed correct (P(error|human)=0). That is optimistic toward the human queue — a real analyst error rate would raise the all-human arm's true cost — so router-vs-all-human comparisons are conservative in the human arm's favor. API cost is INCURRED spend and is charged unconditionally: a policy that defers to a human after paying for a model call still pays for that call, and a policy that defers before any paid call passes api_cost_usd = 0.0 for that example.
